minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  May 19, 2020

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
May 19, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales
  and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency at the hour of 2:05 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary announced the presence of a quorum
as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts/Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Jacquelyn Gordon  Staff Assistant

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council/Successor Agency on any item on the Agenda.

There was no response.

  1
 May 19, 2020

 301  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – ORDINANCE AMENDING THE
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH POLICIES FOR SHORT
  TERM RENTALS. The public hearing was continued to May 26, 2020, at the hour of
  2:00 p.m.

 178  PAYMENT OF INVOICES APPROVED – CELLEBRITE. Staff report dated May
  19, 2020, was presented recommending authorization to pay invoices from Cellebrite for
  mobile device data extraction and analytics services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve payment in the amount of $24,305.01. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 178  PAYMENT OF INVOICES APPROVED – LEVERAGE INFORMATION
  SYSTEMS. Staff report dated May 19, 2020, recommending authorization to pay
  invoices from Leverage Information Systems for repair and maintenance of the Police
  Department’s camera equipment.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve payment in the amount of $16,800.09. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 125  FOURTH AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-055 AND FOURTH
  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-058 WITH REMY MOOSE MANLEY,
  LLP (RMM) – NOT APPROVED

  This item was pulled from the Agenda.

 101  CREATION, DEVELOPMENT AND STAFFING FOR THE HOUSING
  PROTECTION  DEPARTMENT  -  APPROVED;  FINANCE
  DEPARTMENT/BUDGET DIVISION DIRECTED TO CREATE THE
  NECESSARY BUDGET ACCOUNTS TO SUPPORT THE HP DEPARTMENT;
  RESOLUTION NO. 20-066 ADPOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2019-2020 BUDGET; AN ADDITIONAL 10 POSITIONS (TO BE HIRED IN
  PHASES AS NEEDED) DURING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET -
  AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated May 19, 2020, recommending approval to develop
  and staff a Housing Protection Department.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Franklin that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Approve the creation, development and staffing for the HP
  Department; 2) Direct the Finance Department/Budget Division to create the necessary
  budget accounts to support the HP Department; 3) Adopt Resolution No. 20-066 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,CALIFORNIA ESTABLISHING A HOUSING PROTECTION
  DEPARTMENT, AUTHORIZING THE STAFFING OF THE HOUSING
  PROTECTION DEPARTMENT AND AMENDING THE 2019-2020 FISCAL
  YEAR BUDGET TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO ASSIST IN THE INITIAL
  CREATION PHASE AND STAFFING OF THE DEPARTMENT

  and 4) Authorize the hire of an additional 10 positions (to be hired in phases as needed)
  during the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 budget to support the needs of the HP Department,
  pending inclusion in the Salary Ordinance. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and;
  Noes: None.

  2
 May 19, 2020

  It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Rescind the previous motion and action; 2) Approve
  the creation, development and staffing of the HP Department; 3) Direct the Finance
  Department/Budget Division to create the necessary budget accounts to support the HP
  Department; 4) Adopt Resolution Number 20-066 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,CALIFORNIA  ESTABLISHING  A  HOUSING
  PROTECTION DEPARTMENT, AUTHORIZING THE STAFFING OF
  THE HOUSING PROTECTION DEPARTMENT AND AMENDING
  THE 2019-2020 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET TO PROVIDE FUNDING TO
  ASSIST IN THE INITIAL CREATION PHASE AND STAFFING OF
  THE DEPARTMENT

  5) Authorize the hire of an additional 10 positions (to be hired in phases as needed)
  during the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 budget to support the needs of the HP Department,
  pending inclusion in the Salary Ordinance; with an amendment and stipulation that any
  cost associated with this program will be reimbursed to the general fund at a later date, at
  the point that the fees are collected. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  CALIFORNIA TAX CREDIT ALLOCATION COMMITTEE (TCAC) LEASE
  RIDER FOR PATH EUCALYPTUS - APPROVED. Staff report dated May 19, 2020,
  recommending approval of a California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (TCAC) Lease
  Rider for PATH Eucalyptus located at 502-508 S. Eucalyptus Avenue, Inglewood, CA
  90301.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby approve California Tax Credit Allocation Committee
  Lease Rider. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  APPOINTMENTS TO THE HOUSING ADVISORY COMMISSION – RATIFIED.
  Staff report dated May 19, 2020, was presented recommending the appointment and
  confirmation of two Inglewood Housing Authority (IHA) Section 8 tenant participants to
  the Housing Advisory Commission.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that Georgia
  C. Gist-Williams, and Ramsey Jones be appointed to the Housing Advisory Commission
  for the term ending March 2022. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 18-150 - APPROVED; USE OF
  ADDITIONAL ROPS FUNDING - APPROVED. Staff report dated May 19, 2020,
  was presented to recommending approval of an amendment to Agreement No. 18-150
  with Sialic Contractors, Corporation dba Shawnan to increase the contract amount by an
  additional $332,300 for construction work performed on the Imperial Highway
  Improvement Project (P610).

  It was moved by Council Member/Successor Agency Member Franklin, seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member Morales, that the City Council/Successor
  Agency does hereby: 1) Approve amendment; and 2) Approve additional ROPS funding
  in the amount of $332,300 for Project P610. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin
  and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
 May 19, 2020

 125  CLOSED SESSION – ATTORNEY/CLIENT PRIVILEGED; CONFERENCE
  WITH  LABOR  NEGOTIATOR;  NAME  OF  ORGANIZATIONS
  REPRESENTING  EMPLOYEES:  INGLEWOOD  POLICE  OFFICERS
  ASSOCIATION  (IPOA);  INGLEWOOD  POLICE  MANAGEMENT
  ASSOCIATION (IPMA). Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged;
  Conference with Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6:
  Names of the Agency Negotiator: Jose O. Cortes, Human Resources Director: Name of
  Organizations Representing Employees: Inglewood Police Officers Association (IPOA);
  Inglewood Police Management Association (IPMA).

  Discussion Held; Direction Given to Staff.

  219  REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. City Treasurer, Wanda Brown, referenced a March
  10, 2020, City Council Agenda Item from City Manager, Artie Fields regarding a
  resolution to establish an Investment Committee. The City Treasurer commented on her
  recent breast cancer diagnosis, and her current cancer treatment. Wanda Brown,
  commented that since the City’s Inception in 1908, an Investment Committee did not
  exist; however, when she was elected in June 1987, she established the first and only
  Investment Oversight Committee that is not required in Government Code 53600.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in honor of Jerry Freeman, and Larry Albury at the hour of 2:23 p.m.

  Approved this ______day of ___________, 2020

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
